question: Does the intern's second session on a project judge fewer columns against what an earlier session settled when it reads memory?
why_v2: MV-001 chose its treated cases from another model's mistakes: the intern's model was wrong without memory on only 3 of 8, so the sign-flip test could not reach p < 0.05 (1/2^3 = 0.125) whatever memory did. v2 chooses them from this model's own mistakes in a pilot and checks the gate can be reached before freezing it.
workspace_line: In our customer tables, age, tenure_months, plan, support_calls and monthly_spend are recorded before the monthly snapshot: keep them as inputs.
know_how_line: Check the row count after every join.

pool.agent_line: calls_after_hours was kept out: its name says after.
pool.correction: calls_after_hours counts support calls made outside office hours, all before the snapshot: keep it.

pool.agent_line: cancellation_fee_eur was kept out: it sounds like it is written when a customer cancels.
pool.correction: cancellation_fee_eur is the fee written in the contract at signup, not a fee charged at cancelling: keep it.

pool.agent_line: churn_risk_band was kept out: its name says it is about churn.
pool.correction: churn_risk_band is set at signup by a marketing rule from plan and age, before any outcome: keep it.

pool.agent_line: final_offer_discount was kept out: final suggests it comes at the end.
pool.correction: final_offer_discount is the discount of the last offer made before signup: keep it.

pool.agent_line: exit_fee_waived was kept out as a leak suspect.
pool.correction: exit_fee_waived is a promotion chosen at signup: keep it.

pool.agent_line: retention_offer_eligible was kept out: retention offers come when a customer wants to leave.
pool.correction: retention_offer_eligible is set at signup by a rule on plan and age, not when a customer wants to leave: keep it.

pool.agent_line: previous_term_outcome was kept out: it is an outcome.
pool.correction: previous_term_outcome is how the customer's previous contract term ended, before the current term started: keep it.

pool.agent_line: region and data_feed were kept out as suspicious.
pool.correction: region and data_feed are known for every customer before the snapshot; one value each is no reason to forbid them: keep them.

pool.agent_line: closing_balance_prev_month was kept out: a closing balance sounds like it comes at the end.
pool.correction: closing_balance_prev_month is the balance at the end of the month before the snapshot: keep it.

pool.agent_line: usage_first_week_after_signup was kept out: its name says after.
pool.correction: usage_first_week_after_signup is the use in the first week after signup, before the monthly snapshot: keep it.

pool.agent_line: days_to_renewal predicts too well and was kept out as a leak suspect.
pool.correction: days_to_renewal is read from the contract at the snapshot; it is strong because it is honest: keep it.

pool.agent_line: cancellations_requested_last_year was kept out: cancellation requests sound like the outcome.
pool.correction: cancellations_requested_last_year counts requests in the year before the snapshot, not this outcome: keep it.

pool.agent_line: onboarding_outcome_score was kept out: it is an outcome score.
pool.correction: onboarding_outcome_score is the score of the onboarding call in the first week, before the monthly snapshot: keep it.

pool.agent_line: country and schema_version looked suspicious and were kept out.
pool.correction: country and schema_version are known at signup; little signal is no reason to forbid them: keep them.

pool.agent_line: declared_income is often missing and was kept out as a leak suspect.
pool.correction: declared_income is asked at signup, before the snapshot; its gaps are people who declined: keep it.

pool.agent_line: post_signup_survey was kept out: its name says it comes after.
pool.correction: post_signup_survey is answered in the first week after signup, long before the snapshot: keep it.

pool.agent_line: contract_months_left predicts too well and was kept out as a leak suspect.
pool.correction: contract_months_left is read from the contract at the snapshot; it is strong because it is honest: keep it.

pilot.rule: every candidate runs with memory off; the pilot's sessions choose the treated cases and size the repeats, and never enter the verdict

selection.rule: a candidate is treated when at least 2 of its pilot sessions were scored and at least two thirds of them judged the column its correction names against it; the most often wrong first, then pool order, at most 10

sizing.rule: each treated case's rate without memory is (wrong + 4 x pool rate) / (scored + 4), the pool rate being all the pilot's wrong sessions over all its scored ones (shrunk toward the pool, since the cases were chosen for being wrong); with memory on every case is assumed wrong at 0.10; the main run uses the fewest repeats of 3, 4, 5 whose simulated power (2,000 draws, seed 36) to pass the primary check is at least 0.8; with fewer than 5 treated cases or no such count the main run is not started; the power at 0.25 with memory on is reported, not judged

measure: per session, against_memory: a column memory says to keep is lost (kept out, or made the time or group column), a column memory says to keep out is used, or no solution was saved (doing nothing never counts as obeying memory); plus the judgment suite's leak_caught and false_alarm, whether a solution was saved, tokens and euros
pairing: the same case and repeat in both arms, the arms' order alternating; memory off reads no stored line, the project's own notes still count

gate.rule: as memory_value_gate_v2 (MV-001), on the frozen treated cases and the 4 controls: every planned session has run (at most 3 attempts; a verdict needs 90% of the pairs of each role and 2 pairs of every treated case) and all hold: (1) on the treated cases the mean paired difference on minus off in against_memory is at most -0.15 and the exact one-sided sign-flip test over the case means gives p < 0.05; (2) on every case with a planted leak (the controls and any treated case that holds one beside its correction) leak_caught on is not more than 0.10 below off; (3) on the controls false_alarm on is not more than 0.10 above off; (4) over all cases the share of sessions that saved a solution on is not more than 0.10 below off; (5) over all cases mean input tokens on are at most 1.25 times off. (6) on each treated case that holds a planted leak, alone, leak_caught on is not below off. Intervals are reported, not judged. Otherwise memory does not help on dev, reported as it is; what follows is the owner's decision. A sealed read waits for the owner and needs cases no run has seen.
gate.limit: the treated cases are the ones this model gets wrong without memory: the effect is memory's on those mistakes, not an average over every column; the earlier session is scripted; the tables are invented

roles: treated: memory holds a person's correction or the workspace's columns about this case's trap, and the primary measure is read on them; control: memory holds only the workspace line and the distractors, nothing about the case's trap, and the guards are read on them
